findings.what_happened: After almost every action (open step, send answer, keep topics, approve, choose a question) focus drops to the page body or lands on a heading with no visible focus style. The answer box is never focused automatically. My first typed answer went into a collapsed 'What happens in this step' button and was lost. Tab from the body then jumps to an unpredictable control (sometimes the textarea, sometimes the primary button), and the next Tab leaves the panel to the header.
findings.expected: After each action focus moves to the next logical control (the answer box, or the new panel's primary action), with a visible ring. At least the panel heading should show a focus outline.
findings.suggested_fix: Programmatically focus the first interactive control (answer textarea or primary action) after each panel change. Give focused headings a visible outline, or focus the container with a skip hint. Do not let a button that becomes disabled ('Chosen') drop focus to the body.

findings.page: Summary and ranking (/table) after pressing 'Appraise selected papers'
findings.what_happened: After pressing Appraise selected papers and waiting about 14 seconds, the page showed no change: the top bar said step 7/9 but the content was still step 6, the sticky action button vanished and no 'Go to step 7' or progress message appeared. I had to guess that the 'Overview' link would show a way forward, then press 'Go to step 7: Appraisal' there.
findings.expected: Either move to the appraisal step, or show a running state ('Appraising 13 papers...') and a visible next action.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a progress or running banner, then navigate to the appraisal view or show 'Go to step 7' on this page. This also matches the intent doc's 'no page is a dead end'.

findings.page: Scoping approved panel -> 'Go to step 3: Search builder'
findings.what_happened: Pressing 'Go to step 3: Search builder' opened 'Edit this search topic: Peer' (a topic editor) with the header still reading 'Viewing step 2 of 9 - Done'. I thought I had gone to the wrong place and needed to press 'Write the searches' without knowing why.
findings.expected: 'Go to step 3' opens the step-3 search builder overview, labelled step 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Route to the step-3 landing view, or update the header and heading to say this is the first topic's search and that 'Write the searches' creates queries for all topics.

findings.what_happened: After I answered two scoping questions, the summary said 'not answered yet' for every field and '0 of 6 answered', so my answers looked lost. The suggested topics were single words ('Peer', 'Support', 'Groups', 'Postpartum') plus generic 'Measurement and outcomes' and 'Context and setting'. 'Depression' and 'low-income' were missing. The 'Peer' search string contained 'telemedicine' as an index term. None of this is flagged next to the topic.
findings.expected: My answers appear under who, where and outcome, and topics are meaningful concepts (e.g. 'peer support groups', 'postpartum depression', 'low- and middle-income countries'). Any mock substitution is flagged where it appears.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the answers I gave in 'What we know so far'. In demo mode, label the topic and query lists as scripted ('(mock) not derived from your answers') and explain why telemedicine terms appear. In live mode, validate that topics are phrases.

findings.page: Appraisal to Synthesis (step 7 to 8) and Research question
findings.what_happened: The landing page promises every quote is 'checked against its source' and the appraisal asks me to decide 13 unverified quotes, yet I looked at 0 of 13 papers, decided 0 quotes and pressed 'Summarise the evidence' straight through. The synthesis and questions were still built from them. In the one paper I opened, a quote about public uptake of apps was used under 'Risk of bias assessed', so a 'verified' quote did not support its answer. The chosen question is about telemedicine though my idea was postpartum depression, and the report title and question disagree.
findings.expected: Undecided quotes block or clearly warn before synthesis. 'Verified' should say only that the words exist in the text, not that they support the answer. The final report should flag a mismatch between idea and question.
findings.suggested_fix: On 'Summarise the evidence' show 'N quotes still undecided. They will be left out' and require confirmation. Reword the verified badge to 'wording found in text'. In demo mode add a banner inside the report and the research-question step that the question does not match the user's idea.

findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom the password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') overlaps the bottom of the password input and sits over the typed dots, hard to read for low vision. The focus ring surrounds both.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field with space between.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the hint normal flow with margin-top, or make the label/input/hint a column grid with gap; do not position the hint over the input.

findings.page: Step side panel at 200% zoom (all steps)
findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom on a 1366x900 screen the panel's scrollable content area is only about 350-450px high. The header block (title, text, 9-segment strip) and the footer buttons take most of the screen, and the sticky demo note takes more. Lists and cards are viewed through a letterbox, and I often could not see what was focused without scrolling. The paper/ranking pages have a sticky top bar, note and bottom button that leave about half the screen.
findings.expected: Headers shrink or scroll with content at high zoom so the working area is most of the viewport.
findings.suggested_fix: Below roughly 1000px effective width make the panel header non-sticky (scroll away) and collapse the step description. Let the demo note scroll away once seen.

findings.what_happened: Escape closes the drawer correctly and the drawer traps Tab, but focus does not return to the paper row I opened. It falls to the body and the next Tab goes back to 'Skip to content', so I would have to tab through dozens of rows again.
findings.expected: Focus returns to the row that opened the drawer.
findings.suggested_fix: Store document.activeElement before opening the drawer and restore it on close.

findings.what_happened: Each paper has about 30 tab stops (a 'Show source' and 'Pin to canvas' per quality question) before I reach 'Summarise the evidence'. I tabbed about 40 times from the top of the panel with no shortcut. Both footer buttons look similar, so I was unsure which was primary until I found 'Next paper'. 'Click a chip' and 'Click the arrow' hints are mouse-first.
findings.expected: A landmark or skip link to 'Next paper / Summarise' and keyboard-oriented hint wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Skip to actions' inside the panel, collapse per-question buttons into a single disclosure, and word hints as 'select' or 'press Enter'.

findings.what_happened: Console reported a page error 'Failed to execute removeChild on Node: The node to be removed is not a child of this node' when I pressed 'Summarise the papers' while the 3D/2D chart was on the page. The step still worked.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the chart teardown (Three.js or SVG container) for double removal on unmount.

findings.what_happened: The page says the top 3-5 papers per topic are selected, but 'Groups' and 'Context and setting' show 0 selected and the checklist shows '0 of 3 done'. No warning appeared before 'Appraise selected papers'. My Journal-article filter from step 5 silently stayed on ('Showing 29 of 44'), and the filter text was easy to miss. The Overview later said '16 selected' but appraisal listed 13 papers.
findings.expected: A warning when a topic has none, filters reset when entering a new step or announced prominently, and consistent counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Warn about topics with fewer than 3 selected, announce active filters in a live region at the top, and explain 16 vs 13.

findings.what_happened: 'Colour by' offers Study type, Topic and Source database only, so I cannot colour or filter by article type there. Article type appears only as counts, with filters in the later table step. In Topic mode the legend says 'Peer 36, Support 4, Postpartum 4', which implies 36 papers are about peer support when they are demo telemedicine papers. The hint 'hover to highlight' does not mention keyboard focus.
findings.expected: Article type is reachable as a view in the paper list or clearly pointed to. Legend hint mentions keyboard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the hint to 'hover, focus or click'; add a pointer from the article-type counts to the table filters; in demo mode caveat topic counts.

findings.what_happened: The paper header shows '? citations', which reads as broken, and 'Found in pubmed' is lower case.
findings.expected: 'Citation count not available' and 'Found in PubMed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the field when unknown or say 'citation count unavailable'; use proper brand capitalisation.

findings.page: Step 1 / New review and project overview
findings.what_happened: After I typed my idea and pressed 'Start my review', the overview said 'Your next step: Tell us what you want to research - Open step 1', asking me to confirm text I just entered. The example chips sit between the textarea and 'Start my review', costing three extra tabs.
findings.expected: Typing the idea and starting should move on to scoping, with the examples after or out of the tab order before the primary button.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the redundant step-1 confirmation, or reword the step-1 panel to 'Confirm your idea'. Move example chips below the primary button in DOM order.

findings.what_happened: The report is described as 'Markdown, a text document: opens in Word, Google Docs or any text editor.' A Markdown file does not render in Word. After pressing Download there was no visible confirmation or toast, so I could not tell whether it saved. The tab order is fine and the in-page preview with 'first 200 of 799 lines' is helpful.
findings.expected: Honest format wording, and a short 'Download started' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'plain text with simple formatting; paste it into Word or Google Docs' (or offer .docx), and show a live-region message after download.

findings.what_happened: The report's scoping section repeats my 'who' answer as both 'population' and 'setting'. The 'novelty check' lists unrelated results (dementia care, veterinary volunteering, digital pathology) marked 'already in your review'. It is caveated as not proof of novelty, which is good, but it looks odd.
findings.expected: Scoping fields correspond to what I wrote and the novelty list makes sense or is labelled as demo data.
findings.suggested_fix: Map answers to fields correctly, or label unclassified answers; in demo mode, label the novelty list 'sample results'.

three_second_test.note: Heading and two buttons make it clear it turns a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First action is Start a review; skip link and focus ring are visible.
Plain form, but the password hint overlaps the field at 200% zoom.
Describe the idea, then Start my review. The textarea is auto-focused, which is good. Example chips sit in the tab path before the button.
A list with 'Open step 1' for the idea I just typed. I was unsure why I was asked again.
Confirm the idea and press Start scoping, but it duplicates the previous page and the panel fills the screen at 200%.
Answer the question and press Send. Focus is not in the answer box, so my first typing was lost.

three_second_test.page: Keep suggested topics / Use these topics
three_second_test.note: Keep or edit topics then approve. The single-word topics are not understandable as search topics for my subject.
Check searches then Run all 12. The 'telemedicine' term in my 'Peer' query was confusing.
Counts of found and duplicate papers; legend with shapes and counts is clear. Chart reached by keyboard through the legend.
Table of papers with a 3-item checklist and filter chips; chip wording is mouse-oriented.
Focus landed on the bottom button of a long list and the 3-5 per topic rule conflicts with 0 selected in two topics; unclear what to do.
Heavy: many quote cards, 13 undecided quotes and no obvious route. I understood it is a per-paper checklist but not what was required.
Known / contested / unknown with quote chips and a clear 'Suggest research questions' action.
Three candidates with gap, feasibility, weakness and a novelty caveat; Finish and export is locked until choose, which is clear.
Pick a format and download; a preview is shown. Markdown described as opening in Word.

categories_and_colours: Study type has a colour, a shape and a text label in the legend (Trial blue circle, Cohort orange square, Cross-sectional green triangle, Qualitative amber diamond, Systematic/scoping review pink star, Other design green cross, Not reported grey ring). I understood the legend without being told, and unused categories are dimmed. The legend is reachable and operable by keyboard as buttons with counts, and the active article-type filter shows a tick icon as well as a fill, so state is not colour alone. In the table I could filter by study type and by article type (Journal article 29, Review article 6, Preprint 2, Editorial/letter/comment 7), and the page said 'Showing 29 of 44: journal article. 15 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' with a Reset filters button. Problems: (1) at retrieval the Colour by menu has no Article type option and the legend hint says 'hover to highlight', which is mouse-first; (2) the Peer/Support/Postpartum topic colours in the demo imply 36 papers on 'peer', which is misleading; (3) a filter set in step 5 silently persists into step 6; (4) the 3D canvas itself cannot be navigated by keyboard (only the legend and 2D toggle can), though the 2D alternative is offered; (5) the retrieval counts (Not reported 34) differ from the table counts after AI summary (Not reported 12), which is explained in the page text and was not confusing.
validity_assessment: Traceability is strong where it exists: each paper has real DOI/PMID/PMCID links, every appraisal answer has a quote, and 'Show source' opens the paper text with the exact quote highlighted. The novelty check carries the caveat 'Finding none does not prove a question is new.' The demo-mode note is honest and mock text is labelled '(mock)'. The workflow is not yet valid as a review in demo mode: topics did not use my answers, the retrieved papers are telemedicine and teledentistry, the chosen question is about telemedicine, and the report title and question disagree. More importantly, the process does not enforce its own checks: I advanced from appraisal to synthesis with 0 of 13 flagged quotes decided and 0 papers looked at, two topics had no selected papers, and a 'verified' quote can sit under a question it does not answer (word-for-word found is not the same as supports). Statements like 'every quote checked against its source' on the landing page need softening or these gates need enforcing. In live mode I cannot say, but the UI would need the topic extraction and gating fixed to be defensible. Nothing looked fabricated beyond the declared mock data, though the 'Placeholder contradiction... generated to demo' in synthesis shows invented conflicts in demo.
would_have_quit_at: Step 6 to 7 (Ranking, then Appraisal). After pressing 'Appraise selected papers' nothing happened on the page for 14 seconds and the sticky button disappeared, so a real user would likely give up or reload. The 200% zoom letterbox, focus loss after each step and the 30-tab-stops-per-paper appraisal would also wear down a keyboard-only user before step 7.
activity: Created one account (ruth.lecturer.qa1@example.com) and one project (prj_5ab3567e15e24b86) titled 'Peer support groups for postpartum depression in low-income countries'. Answered 2 of 5 scoping questions, skipped the rest, kept 6 suggested topics, ran all 12 searches (44 unique papers), summarised the papers (4 batches), ranked, appraised (13 papers), synthesised (12 statements, 4 conflicts), chose candidate 1 and finished the export. Toggled the 2D chart and Colour by, filtered the table by article type (Journal article), opened one paper drawer, and used 'Show source' on one quote. Opened the report preview (200 of 799 lines) and activated the 'Download the report (Markdown)' link. Used about 130 helper commands, all keyboard-only (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, ArrowDown, type). One console page error seen: 'removeChild: The node to be removed is not a child of this node' on summarise. No failed network requests. Screenshots 01-40 saved under docs/qa/iteration-1/keyboard/. Browser stopped.
narrative: I started with the landing page and understood it straight away: turn a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. Tab revealed a skip link, then Log in, then Start a review, each with a clear white focus ring. At sign-up the password hint was printed on top of the password box at 200% zoom, which was hard for me to read, but the form worked and I was taken to step 1 with the textarea already focused, which I liked. After Start my review I was shown a project overview asking me to open step 1 and confirm the idea I had just typed, which felt like a repeat. From there my keyboard journey got harder. After nearly every action, focus fell to the page body and Tab went somewhere unpredictable. I typed my scoping answer while focus was on a collapsed button and lost it, then found that the page's 'what we know so far' said nothing was answered. The search topics were single words and the 'Peer' search mentioned telemedicine. The side panel at 200% zoom left only a narrow strip to read, and the ranking-to-appraisal step seemed to hang with no message. I found 'Overview' and a Go to step 7 button to continue. The appraisal had about thirty tab stops per paper, but 'Show source' with a highlighted quote was excellent for trust. I got through synthesis, chose a question and reached the export, where the preview and download worked, though the question was about telemedicine and there was no download confirmation. The demo note was honest throughout.
